name: Conviction Partners
identity_check: Confirmed as Conviction Partners (conviction.com; Embed programme at embed.conviction.com), the AI-focused early-stage VC firm Sarah Guo founded after leaving Greylock, launched October 2022 with a ~$100M first fund; Mike Vernal (ex-Sequoia) joined as GP in January 2025 alongside a $230M Fund II. Usually written 'Conviction'; press also uses 'Conviction Partners', 'Conviction Capital' (SiliconANGLE, for Sunday and Didero, both of which the firm lists or which name Sarah Guo's firm) and 'Conviction Embed'. Office in San Francisco's Mission District (Colossus). Not 'Conviction Capital' as a separately named firm, and not other similarly named investors; every round below was matched to this firm by the portfolio list on conviction.com, a Sarah Guo quote, or the Embed label.

thesis_text.value: AI-native ('Software 3.0') firm that backs technical founders early, often as the first investor, across the intelligence stack: chips, data infrastructure, developer tools, research labs and AI-native applications in every vertical. It argues AI's impact is still underestimated, works hands-on on talent, customers, data and compute access, and builds community through Embed, fellowships and its podcasts.

open_items: Third fund / expansion vehicles: Colossus (Jul 2026) says three funds totalling nearly $1B; an AltAssets headline (Mar 2026, via pulse.bot) says Conviction was raising a third fund and a second expansion vehicle, implying a first expansion vehicle exists. The pulse.bot page refused connections, guessed AltAssets URLs returned 404, and SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent, so names, sizes and close dates are unknown.
Forbes' 2022-10-04 launch article (exact Fund I announcement date) returned 403.
Company LinkedIn page: conviction.com does not link one, so none recorded. Partner LinkedIn URLs: the site links only Jedd Horowitz's; Guo, Vernal, Reddy and Garcia-Camargo link to X profiles.

Titles for Pranav Reddy, Bella Garcia-Camargo and Jedd Horowitz are not on the site (it lists 'People' without titles); Colossus says the firm is eight people, four of whom invest, and calls Reddy Guo's earliest hire. Partner focus_sectors are classified from the deals each wrote up or was quoted on (Reddy: Latent, Sola; Garcia-Camargo and Vernal: Corridor; Guo: Onyx, Sunday, Baseten); the firm does not assign sectors.

application_url is the Embed application form; the main fund has no form, only 'please reach out' plus a contact email (not recorded). Embed runs in cohorts of 10-12 companies with a mandatory in-person weekend in San Francisco; the page asks for applications to the 7th cohort but its body still says 'three cohorts so far' (stale text). Colossus says Embed has run twice a year since 2023 and picks about a dozen teams from roughly 1,000 applications.
Embed standard terms: $250K on an uncapped, no-discount MFN SAFE (or at the price of a round in the last 60 days), plus $350K AWS and $350K Azure credits and $500K+ of other compute/API credits.
requires_us_entity: not stated. Portfolio includes Mistral (France) and Onyx (New York / Tel Aviv); Colossus describes Embed founders flown in from Vancouver, Tel Aviv, London and Tallinn.
invests_in_indian_founders: nothing stated on any fetched page.
portfolio_count_reported: the firm states no count; conviction.com lists 22 companies 'and others still in stealth'.
HQ: no street address published; San Francisco comes from Colossus (office in the Mission District) and Dakota. Colossus also mentions a Palo Alto office shared with Andrej Karpathy.

Rounds not recorded for lack of a fetched page describing the round with Conviction named: Latent (Forbes 2026-03-18 returned 403; Latent's releases say $80M raised from Transformation Capital, Spark Capital, Conviction, General Catalyst, YC); Baseten (Colossus says Conviction led the 2022 Series A and co-led a $1.5B Series F in 2026); Sunday's $35M from Benchmark and Conviction (Nov 2025, mentioned only in SiliconANGLE's Series B story); Trajectory (site shows $15M, 'Backed by Conviction'); Distributed Spectrum, Quadrillion, Instinct, Harvey, Mistral, Cognition, Sierra, HeyGen, Cartesia, OpenEvidence.

Onyx's March 2026 launch round: a search-result hint said $35M Series A led by Conviction; the fetched release says only '$40M in funding from Conviction and Cyberstarts', so it is recorded with stage undisclosed and no lead.

Didero's $30M Series A (Feb 2026, led by Chemistry and Headline) does not name Conviction; only the 2024 seed does. Listen Labs announced it is joining Salesforce (2026-09-29) and Corridor is joining Cognition; these exits are not recorded as rounds.

Parallax Worlds pre-seed: amount and date not disclosed (implied ~$0.9M as $4.9M total less the $4M seed). Watchtower Labs and alphaXiv websites and HQs not stated on the fetched pages. Listen Labs Series B round size not stated (total funding $100M).

Press names vary: 'Conviction Capital' (SiliconANGLE: Sunday, Didero), 'Conviction Partners' (Enigma, Keenable), 'Conviction Embed' / 'Conviction (Embed)' (alphaXiv, Parallax Worlds); all matched to this firm via its portfolio list, the Embed label or Sarah Guo.
